clue.text: Opening heart, perhaps, and play this

parts.note: an opening such as the one in your face you speak through is a mouth
the heart is one example of a bodily organ, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: Reads like a stage direction: open your heart and perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like a verb but is a noun, the mouth; 'heart, perhaps' is an organ given by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is an instrument a player blows into, so 'play this' points at it.

clue.text: Complaints mature in case of grievances

indicators.note: in places the word for mature inside the outer letters of grievances
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: fruit that is mature is ripe

explanation.surface: Grown-up complaints wrapped in a bundle of grievances.
explanation.definitionFit: Gripes is an informal plural noun for grumbles or complaints.

clue.text: Argued with leader going for speakers ultimately with experience

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for argued is swapped out for a new one

parts.note: to have argued a case logically is to have reasoned

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of speakers

explanation.surface: A debater who argued, with a new leader, ends up among experienced speakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with leader going for' swaps the R at the front of REASONED for S, the last letter of 'speakers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone seasoned is hardened and practised, having plenty of experience.

clue.text: Such clues may be an affliction

parts.note: a cross to bear is a burden or affliction

explanation.surface: A self-referential grumble that crossword clues can be a torment.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the clue itself: this clue is a down clue, but such clues as the other half of the grid are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The across clues are one of the two sets of crossword clues, a playful self-reference.

clue.text: Wide bridges needing time and funds

parts.note: W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a wide
arches are the curved spans that bridges rest on

explanation.surface: Building wide bridges takes time and money.
explanation.definitionFit: A war chest is a fund of money set aside for a campaign.

clue.text: Care assistants will accept penalties given here

indicators.note: the words care assistants will accept, holding within them, a run of letters spanning the gap

explanation.surface: Care workers being willing to accept fines.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a penalty is awarded for a foul in the penalty area, the box in front of goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Penalties are given for fouls in the penalty area of a football pitch, so this is a cryptic description of that zone.

clue.text: Son needs guts, ignoring a cause of great suffering

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out the letter a from the word for guts

parts.note: guts is informal for bravery or courage

explanation.surface: A son needing pluck but ignoring something that causes suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring a' drops the first A of COURAGE, leaving COURGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a whip, and figuratively a person or thing causing widespread misery.

clue.text: Pointed performance included in cost is cheating

parts.note: something with a fine point is sharp

indicators.note: included in puts the word for performance inside the word for cost

parts.note: the cost of something is its price
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A barbed show whose price turns out to be a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp practice is dishonest dealing that stops just short of being illegal.

clue.text: Irritation caused by hollow cough and a smile

indicators.note: a hollow word has its insides emptied, leaving only the outer letters of cough

parts.note: a broad smile is a grin

explanation.surface: Annoyance at someone who coughs emptily and then grins.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation or annoyance, especially at one's own failure or humiliation.

clue.text: Horologists must support free thing for such workers

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath the other piece
free means the letters of thing are set loose and rearranged

parts.note: horologists make watches, so they are watchmen in the playful sense

explanation.surface: Clockmakers are obliged to back some liberated object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges THING into NIGHT; 'must support' puts WATCHMEN below it, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Night-watchmen are guards working the night shift, the workers the clue describes.

clue.text: Points at a silly starter course

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters of points at a are jumbled into nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone gestures at a foolish first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian appetiser of cured meats and olives served before the main meal.

clue.text: Noise from family group beginning to grate

parts.note: a clan is a group of related families

indicators.note: beginning to points to the opening letter of grate

explanation.surface: A family starts to irritate with its racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a loud ringing metallic sound, a kind of noise.

clue.text: Common resources may see sailing vessel return

indicators.note: return means the word for the sailing vessel comes back the other way, read from the end

parts.note: a sloop is a single-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: Shared assets might mean a yacht coming home.
explanation.definitionFit: Pools are shared reserves of money or resources that several people draw on.

clue.text: Shelter from sun then is unusual

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of sun then is are rearranged into an odd order

explanation.surface: Shade from the sun is then a rarity.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nissen hut is a prefabricated half-cylinder of corrugated iron, a wartime shelter.

clue.text: Writing bound to be a feat of athleticism

parts.note: a person's hand is their handwriting
to bound is to leap, and a leap is a spring

explanation.surface: Writing tied up as a gymnastic achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'tied' or 'obliged' but is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A handspring is a gymnastic move flipping over onto the hands and back to the feet.

clue.text: Scold daughter about tiny plant that causes hay fever

indicators.note: about here means in attendance on, so daughter is placed beside tiny, after it

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease or scold them
wee is Scottish and informal for tiny

explanation.surface: Telling off a daughter about a tiny allergenic weed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragweed is a plant whose abundant pollen is a leading trigger of hay fever.

clue.text: Strange metal boxes people used for cheese

indicators.note: boxes means the jumbled metal encloses the word for people
strange signals that the letters of metal are rearranged

parts.note: men is a common crossword word for people

explanation.surface: Odd metal containers holding people, used for cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' turns METAL into EMTAL, which 'boxes' MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmental is a Swiss cheese famous for its large holes.

clue.text: An amount of money reportedly for a dish?

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are spoken, so we go by how they are said

parts.note: taken as written; a tenner is a ten-pound note, an amount of money in British slang

explanation.surface: Asking the price of a dish, said to be ten quid.
explanation.walkthrough: A TENNER is British slang for a ten-pound note; 'an tenner' in a non-rhotic accent sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite dish is one type of aerial, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Welcomes allegations — under a cloud at first

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the word for allegations below the other pieces
at first points to the opening letter of cloud

parts.note: claims are assertions or allegations

explanation.surface: Someone under suspicion greets the accusations against them.
explanation.definitionFit: To acclaim is to hail or greet with enthusiastic praise, so the plural verbs match.

clue.text: Commander-in-Chief must arrest poor inmate filming?

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so the abbreviation captures the jumbled prisoner
poor signals the letters of inmate in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A top commander must detain a wretched prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation C-in-C, written CIC, is split by the rearranged prisoner: 'must arrest' holds it, 'poor' signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinematic means relating to films, so it describes something to do with filming, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Form of street canopy

indicators.note: a form of a word is a reshaping of the letters of street

explanation.surface: Something like a street awning.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester is a canopy over a four-poster bed or pulpit.

clue.text: Notes consequences

definitions.meaning: musical notes together make up a tune
to face the ... is to accept the consequences of one's actions

explanation.surface: A memo's outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes make up a piece played; and in the idiom 'face the music' it stands for unpleasant consequences.

clue.text: Ponder broadcast and slip inside for some breakfast

indicators.note: broadcast scatters the letters of the word for ponder

parts.note: to muse is to ponder

indicators.note: inside takes the inner letters of slip

explanation.surface: Think about a radio programme and slip something into your breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like a sound signal but here scatters the letters of the word for ponder; 'inside' takes the inner pair of 'slip'.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a breakfast cereal of oats, nuts and dried fruit.

clue.text: Article written by Channel island statesman?

indicators.note: written by places the article right beside the island, after it

parts.note: IOW is the abbreviation for the Isle of Wight, an island in the English Channel
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An essay written by someone from a Channel island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel island' suggests Jersey or Guernsey, but it is the Isle of Wight (IOW), off England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iowan comes from the US state of Iowa, so is literally a man of a state.

clue.text: Shed tears seeing moderate Tory embracing party's leader

indicators.note: embracing means the word for moderate Tory holds the next piece inside

parts.note: a wet is a moderate Conservative, a term from the Thatcher era

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Weeping at the sight of a centrist Conservative hugging the party chief.
explanation.walkthrough: A WET was a Thatcher-era label for a moderate Conservative (Tory) politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To weep is to shed tears, and the past tense matches.

clue.text: Caught short and this may be beaten

parts.note: an animal caught in a trap has been snared
a short is a small measure of spirit, such as rum

explanation.surface: Someone caught short and beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught short' looks like the idiom for needing a toilet; here 'short' is a spirit drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is a drum struck with sticks, so it is beaten.

clue.text: Pay for former head to tour Italy

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-partner

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so the word for head goes round the country's letter

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A retired boss pays for a trip round Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: To expiate a sin is to atone or make amends for it, paying the price.

clue.text: Sort of pigment required by working lineman

indicators.note: working means the letters of lineman are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A pigment that a busy telephone engineer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Melanin is the dark pigment in skin, hair and eyes.
